# Itiha intelligence brief, 2026-11-23

**Today is the publish day for the Guru Tegh Bahadur Short and the last day for Tipu Sultan, whose English readership rose to 2.64x its usual as the row reached street protests in Latur. Neither has a script on disk. The Sonia Gandhi Short failed its day-three test, so recent-politics Shorts come off the list.**

## This week: 3 decisions
1. **Script and publish a Short on Aurangzeb's order to execute Guru Tegh Bahadur, for 24 November.** (short, due 2026-11-24, open since 2026-11-15)  
   Why: Tomorrow is the date, the top one in the calendar, and it names Aurangzeb, the villain of the channel's two largest videos. Breakouts are the lever furthest behind: 0 subscribers from them this month against 1,722 planned. It rests on the date and the name, so judge it on search views over the year, not on its third day.  
   First step: No script is on disk yet: write and record it now. Open on Sis Ganj in Chandni Chowk, then Aurangzeb's order, an act of state. Title starts “Guru Tegh Bahadur”. Publish 17:00 IST today, or by 10:00 IST tomorrow.
2. **Script, record and publish one Tipu Sultan Short on the fall of Srirangapatna in 1799: who took the treasure, and who wrote his story afterwards.** (short, due 2026-11-20, open since 2026-11-15)  
   Why: It lapses tomorrow, and the moment grew overnight: Tipu Sultan's English Wikipedia readership is up to 2.64x its 30-day median, and on 22 November BJP workers protested in Latur against a Congress MLA's Tipu remarks. The owner's own pick of 15 November. It is second only because Tegh Bahadur's date cannot move.  
   First step: Once Tegh Bahadur is up. Open on the line his admirers use, in their words, then the record of who took his treasure in 1799. Publish tonight, or press Drop with a one-line note.
3. **Script and publish a follow-up long-form for the Indonesia video's viewers: why Bali stayed Hindu when Java converted.** (long, due 2026-12-02, open since 2026-11-19)  
   Why: The Indonesia long-form brings 3.6 subscribers per 1,000 views against 2 for the bigger Asia one, on 90,680 views, and viewers from Indonesia are still writing in. Its daily views are falling, so the follow-up should land while they still arrive. The Bali topic is a guess from those comments.  
   First step: Put the Indonesia transcript in the long-form scripts folder today so its drop-off check can run. Then the sources: Majapahit's fall and the priests who moved to Bali. Name a culprit and a date, not a religion.

Everything below is the evidence. Mark a decision done or dropped on the Brief tab; an open one stays here until then.

## Channel health
18,200 subscribers, up 700 in a week, against 100,000 by 28 September 2027. November's milestone is 20,364, which needs 76.7 net a day; the last 7 days ran at 114.3. Projection basis: 28-day rate; the 7-day rate is a spike, so the week is not carried forward: the month ends near 18,592, 1,772 short, and the channel is 1,586 behind the ramp today. Only 48.4% of net subscribers over 28 days came from videos; the rest is tied to no video and can stop without warning. The lever furthest behind is breakouts, 0 against 1,722 this month; one video of the usual breakout size (1,396 subscribers) would close most of the month. For a second week what shipped was the owner's own pick (the British officers' pay Short, 22 November), not the list, so the list stays at the two dated Shorts and the Bali follow-up.

What's working
- “How the Ramayana Was REWRITTEN to Convert Hindus” carried long-form this week: long-form views rose 18.0% week over week, and the video has 90,680 views in 5 days. New long-forms have brought 555 subscribers this month against 105 planned, and over 28 days long-form earns 83.3% of upload net subscribers.
- The best converter in the 90-day window is still “How One Man Who Never Visited India Wrote Its History”, at 13.3 net subscribers per 1,000 views: a villain convicted by his own record, then the people still repeating his version. That is the Tipu Short's shape: who took the treasure, then who wrote the story.
- The British officers' pay Short (22 November) is liked by 8.5% of its viewers against a Shorts median of 3.9%. It is on its first day, so judge it on 25 November.

What's wrong
- Neither dated Short has a script on disk, and the slot went to the owner's own pick again. Probable cause: the owner's own scripts are the ones that get recorded. Test: none, it is a choice; today it has to be Tegh Bahadur, because the date will not move.
- The Sonia Gandhi Short failed its day-three test: 912 views at 13.2 an hour and 0 subscribers per 1,000. The script was not the problem: those who saw it watched 77.5% of it on average. Probable cause: Shorts on recent politics land below the usual here, and a book in the news did not change that. Test done: recent-politics Shorts stay off the list.
- Each long-form view is getting shorter: views rose 18.0% week over week but watch time only 1.6%, and the 7-day average view is 27.3%. All three Ramayana long-forms lose most viewers in their first third. Probable cause: Home-feed plays that are not real viewing; 41.6% of November's long-form views were engaged. Test: the Indonesia transcript in the scripts folder, so the check shows where its viewers left before the Bali script is written.
- Shorts views fell 78.5% week over week to 2026-11-20: the Ravana film Shorts' run of 11 November has left the window and nothing dated has gone up since. Search is no longer where most Shorts views come from (30.8% over 28 days). Test: the Tegh Bahadur Short's search views over the coming weeks.

## Audience
Analytics runs to 2026-11-20. Long-form is watched from the Home feed (222,003 views over 28 days, against 6,217 from search) and Shorts from the Shorts feed (157,444, against 81,922 from search).
- Across the niche, comments peak between 18:00 and 22:00 IST, most on Fridays and Saturdays. Publishing at 17:00 IST puts a Short's first hour inside that window, which is why Tegh Bahadur goes up at 17:00.
- The Indonesia video's audience is abroad, Muslim and Buddhist as well as Hindu: viewers from Java, Myanmar and Guyana write in, and several correct details. Meanwhile much of the anger under it has moved from the rewrite to Islam as a whole. A follow-up that names a culprit and a date, not a religion, keeps the first group and gives the second nothing to run with.
- Outside YouTube, WhatsApp is the source that matters: 12,714 views over the 365-day window, against 461 from Instagram. The videos people forward are the ones that correct a record, such as “Why ONLY Hindu Temples Pay Tax in India” and “How Goa Survived 250 Years of the Inquisition”.

## How they are reacting
The Indonesia long-form still holds the week's comments. New this week: a long fact-check saying several supporting facts are wrong, and anger that has turned from the rewrite to Islam as a whole. Under the Asia video the Chola objection is still the top comment.
- **A fact-check of the Indonesia video** (negative): "Its striking facts are mostly real, but several supporting facts are wrong"
- **Anger turning on Islam as a whole** (negative): "Lol allah need ramayan to become popular"
- **Viewers abroad who grew up with the Ramayana** (positive): "I'm a Burmese and Buddhist from my home country Myanmar but still big fan of Ramayana"
- **Conversion still happening today** (negative): "This is still happening in my birth country Guyana to poor people."
- **The Chola objection under the Asia video** (mixed): "“Never sent a single soldier…” ever heard of Chola Empire?"

Requested topics
- Hindi versions of the long-forms (“aap hindi mee bhi video banao na”, under the Indonesia one)
- A Krishna video in the shape of the Asia Ramayana one
- Bagan and the Ramayana in Myanmar

## Competitors
The watchlist's big Shorts this month are still about the Ramayana film, and they went up in the film's first week. The month's best long-form on the watchlist, SHIVOHAM's Subhadra video, opens on a place everyone knows and asks who a familiar figure really is.
- **Project SHIVOHAM**: "She's NOT Subhadra? The Forgotten Ancient Goddess"
  Why it worked: 261,978 views at 10x the channel's median, a long-form. It opens at Puri Jagannath on the three figures millions worship, asks who the goddess between them is, gives the answer everyone knows, then: “But what if the answer is not so simple?”
  Steal: The Bali opening: start on a picture viewers already hold (Bali's temples, its Ramayana dance), ask why the island is still Hindu, give the answer everyone assumes, then turn.
- **The Sham Sharma Show**: "Ranbir Kapoor as Parshuram was"
  Why it worked: 1,448,740 views at 9.6x the median, posted 7 November, in the film's first week. The channel's own film Shorts did best on 10 and 11 November and fell away after.
  Steal: Timing for the two films of 4 December: if either turns out to be a real historical subject, its Short goes up between 5 and 13 December, not later.
- **Nikita Thakur**: "Why is West India Richer than East😳"
  Why it worked: 2,432,202 views at 9.7x the median, a Hindi Short: a why-question about something every viewer lives with, East India rich under the ground and poor above it.
  Steal: The question, answered from the colonial record: the 1793 law that fixed Bengal's land tax for ever (see the first idea below).

Gaps
- “What do Hindus Think of the Abrahamic God?” (The Emissary) has no equivalent on the channel, and the Indonesia video's commenters are arguing that very question. Not for this week.

## Trending now, make this
- **today, short, 3/5**: Guru Tegh Bahadur, 24 November  
  Signal: Tomorrow, the top date in the calendar; the searched phrase is “guru tegh bahadur history”. No script is on disk. (Calendar, decision)  
  Make: Publish today at 17:00 IST, titled with his name first. Judge it on its search views over the year, not on its third day.
- **today, short, 3/5**: Tipu Sultan: the row moved to the street  
  Signal: English Wikipedia readership at 2.64x its 30-day median, 2,980 a day over three days, up from yesterday. On 22 November BJP workers protested in Latur against Congress MLA Amit Deshmukh's Tipu remarks (Mid-Day, ThePrint); on 21 November The Hindu reported his descendant's call for official celebrations. (Wikipedia pageviews, news, decision)  
  Make: Publish tonight after Tegh Bahadur as “Tipu Sultan's Death: Who Got Rich From It”, or press Drop. The decision lapses tomorrow either way.
- **this_week, short, 3/5**: Winston Churchill's birth anniversary, 30 November  
  Signal: Seven days out, and the recording step falls today. His English Wikipedia readership is at its usual level, so this rests on the date alone. (Calendar)  
  Make: Next onto the list when Tipu's place frees tomorrow: one Short on the Bengal famine of 1943 convicted from British papers (War Cabinet minutes, Leo Amery's diary), published 30 November. The channel's earlier Churchill Short lost its viewers to a context dump; its lesson: “The one-sentence context rule applies inside the first 10 seconds most of all.”
- **watch, short, 3/5**: Bentinck's sati regulation, 4 December 1829  
  Signal: 11 days out; the research step is due now. The channel's earlier Short, “How Missionaries Turned Sati Into a Fundraiser”, brought one subscriber, and a commenter there gave the sharper angle: the people who burned witches in Europe stopped sati in India. (Calendar, comments, scripts on disk)  
  Make: Watch, not yet a decision. Check whether the wife-selling script on disk (written 17 September, not recorded) is still unpublished; if so it fits this date on the same hypocrisy. Every claim checked before recording.

## Topic ideas (voltage-checked)
- [3/5, long] **Why Is East India Poorer Than the West? The 1793 Law**  
  Empire and extraction: the Permanent Settlement fixed Bengal's land tax for ever in 1793 and put the land in the hands of revenue collectors; Reframe: a regional gap people blame on themselves runs back to a Company decision; A named culprit with a dated act for the first sentence: Lord Cornwallis, 22 March 1793  
  source: Nikita Thakur's Hindi Short asking the question is at 9.7x her median. Scholarship to start from: Banerjee and Iyer (2005) on landlord and non-landlord districts. Same land tax as the British officers' pay Short of 22 November. A guess, not tested on this channel; check every date before scripting.
- [2/5, short] **The One Time India DID Send an Army to Southeast Asia**  
  Contested history: answers the top comment under the channel's biggest video, which says India never sent a soldier; Trade and empire: the usual explanation for Rajendra Chola's raid on Srivijaya in 1025 is the toll Srivijaya took on the strait Indian ships had to pass  
  source: Top comment under “Why Does All of Asia Know the Ramayana?”. Start from Rajendra's Tanjore inscription, which lists the ports taken. A Short that answers a comment is a guess here, not a tested shape.

## Instagram (separate platform, separate audience)
Instagram has 25,546 followers, up 215 in 7 days, 30.7 a day. The British officers' pay reel has reached 128 so far with a 51.1% skip rate, worse than the level breakout reels stay under. Carousels still grow the account: their median reach is 3.7x that of reels.

Do more
- Build every carousel at 7-10 cards  
  The median carousel in the 7-10 band converts 36 followers (90 posts); outside the band, 12 (16 posts). Pooled rate 2.97 vs 1.85 follows per 1k reach — the band is not just reaching more people, it converts better per person reached, so this is not a reach artefact. 420 followers a month at stake.
- Write carousels that correct the record  
  50 revision carousels in the band converted a median 53.5 followers against 21.5 for the other lanes (40 posts). Median reach 15.9k vs 11.8k, conversion 3.77 vs 2.12 per 1k. 403 followers a month at stake.

Do less
- Stop making posts that get shared without bringing followers  
  17 of 104 rated posts are shared above the median (24.9/1k) but convert below it (2.1/1k): median 11.1k reach for a median 10 followers. The 35 posts that do both average 278 followers each. Share rate and follow rate correlate at only 0.39 — shareable and followable are separate skills, and the first one flatters itself on the home screen. 874 followers a month at stake.
- Stop posting single images  
  87 single images all time: 84.0k reach between them and 120 followers, 1.4 per post. A carousel in the 7-10 band averages 159.6. Every image slot is a carousel slot not taken. 92 followers a month at stake.

## Housekeeping
- **this_week**: Test a new title and the designer's thumbnail on “The Church That Ran Britain's PRISON Camps” in Studio's Test & Compare.  
  Over the 365-day window it brings 34.2 subscribers per 1,000 views, the best on the channel, on only 1,081 views: the people who find it subscribe, and too few find it. That the title is the reason is a guess.
- **this_week**: Upload the Malay Ramayana Short (Ravana getting his powers from Allah) on 25 or 26 November, title starting “Ravana”, with the Indonesia long-form as its related video.  
  The script is written and cut, and it was made to send viewers to the Indonesia long-form, which has averaged 658 views an hour since it went up. That it sends viewers on is a guess.
- **this_week**: If not done yet, answer the two correction comments under the Indonesia long-form, the Majapahit one and the long fact-check, with sources (/replies drafts them).  
  Both sit high on a video still bringing viewers, and the Bali script has to survive the same readers.
- **later**: Check in Studio why “How Jati's evolve organically ?” still has 19 views since 3 November.  
  A public Short gets at least a few views a day; this points to a visibility setting or a restriction, not the topic.
- **later**: Set GA4_PROPERTY_ID in .env so the brief can read itiha.info's traffic.  
  Search Console alone is thin: Google impressions for the site fell sharply from September to October, and every query that shows is the brand name.
